changed.title: Some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 5 gates represents one of two named 5 by 5 graphs (masks 16235582, 16236078) on the one-a-side promise
changed.statement:
∃ M ∈ ([16235582, 16236078] : List ℕ), ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 5 ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => M.testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: whether a NOT gate can save more than 2n - 5 gates on the one-a-side promise at side 5, on the two graphs the read-once count leaves open; a met step breaks the 2n - 5 pair there.
changed.context: No witness is known to us; this is a search; two NOT gates or an input read twice are possible here. Give a gate list of at most 5 AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two for one of the two masks, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. Each graph needs at least 11 gates without NOT gates (checked floors: the 'at most 10 AND/OR' rows read refuted). The other twenty masks of the first break step are covered by a separate 'none exists' form. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

changed.title: The 5 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 32435687 (the crown with one cell removed) has an AND/OR circuit of fan-in two with at most 14 gates on the promise
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 5) (v : Fin 5) => (32435687 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 14
changed.unlocks: whether one named graph sits on or under the open pair's line on the AND/OR side
changed.context: A search. We hold an AND/OR circuit of 15 gates (the crown less a cell in at most 4n - 5, at n = 5; computed). The crown itself costs exactly 15 (a checked row), and the removed cell drops one AND term that the crown's chain shares, so its prefix ORs may serve the cut row with one gate fewer; at side 4 the least value was one below the hand move. What a circuit of 14 decides: by checked rows alone, nothing (a saving of at most 14 - 8 = 6); with the n + m - 2 transfer, a conjecture, it puts the graph on or under the line. We hold no circuit of 14 gates; this is a search.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: two row ORs merged at a column meeting one row and missing the other force another reader, fan-in-two AND/OR circuits
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (u v : Fin n) (c : Fin m)
    (i j : Fin C.gates.length) (p q : ℕ),
  let g := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  let wire := fun idx : Fin C.gates.length => n + m + idx.val
  let isOr := fun (z : Fin C.gates.length) (a b : ℕ) =>
    (g z.val).op = .or ∧ ((g z.val).inputs = [a, b] ∨ (g z.val).inputs = [b, a])
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  u ≠ v → i ≠ j → isOr i u.val p → isOr j v.val q →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.gates.length) u.val = 1 →
  C.output ∉ [u.val, wire i] → G u c = true → G v c = false →
  (C.wires (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach v c)).getD (wire i) false = false ∧
    ∀ t : Fin C.gates.length, isOr t (wire i) (wire j) →
      ∃ h : Fin C.gates.length, h ≠ t ∧ wire i ∈ (g h.val).inputs
changed.unlocks: one step of the count of names against literals on the one-a-side promise, where two row gates merge; it rests on the checked domination row and moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. Compare (u,c) with (v,c), where c meets u and misses v. Except for u, wire values stay ordered until I, since I alone reads u. If I were on at (v,c), the order would continue to the output, a contradiction. If OR T of I,J alone read I, every path from u to the output would pass T. T is on throughout row v via J. Domination gives row containment, contradicted by c. Thus a different gate reads I.
